what.text: Melanotan II (MT-II) is a lab-made peptide: a ring-shaped chain of seven amino acids, modelled on alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (alpha-MSH), a natural hormone that darkens skin. It was made at the University of Arizona and tested there in people in the 1990s.

src.label: Dorr RT, et al. Life Sci 1996

what.text: It switches on melanocortin receptors. In its first study in people it darkened the skin and also caused spontaneous erections, which is why it was then studied for erectile dysfunction (ED).

src.label: Dorr RT, et al. Life Sci 1996
Wessells H, et al. J Urol 1998

what.text: Two related peptides are approved medicines. Bremelanotide is FDA approved as Vyleesi, an injection for low sexual desire in premenopausal women. Afamelanotide is approved for a few medical uses. Neither is Melanotan II.

what.text: Melanotan II is not an approved medicine in any country we checked. It is sold online labelled “for research use only.”

research.text: The human evidence is three small studies from the University of Arizona, with 3 to 10 men each, run between 1996 and 2000. No larger trial has been published. One Phase II trial in vitiligo was registered in 2026 and has no results. Most other published reports on Melanotan II in people are case reports of harm.

research.title: First test in people, 1996

facts.v: single-blind, placebo-controlled; Melanotan II or saline injections under the skin on alternating days
2 weeks, injections Monday to Friday, with rising doses

research.found: Two of the three men had darker skin on the face, upper body and buttocks a week after the last dose. Spontaneous erections came 1 to 5 hours after dosing, with stretching and yawning. Mild nausea occurred at most doses, and one man had moderate sleepiness and fatigue at the highest dose.

src.label: Dorr RT, et al. Life Sci 1996

research.title: Men with psychogenic ED, 1998

facts.v: double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover; one injection of Melanotan II or placebo
10 men with ED of no known physical cause
single doses; erections recorded for 6 hours

research.found: Erections developed in 8 of the 10 men on Melanotan II. Time with strong tip rigidity averaged 38 minutes on Melanotan II and 3 minutes on placebo. Nausea, stretching and yawning, and less appetite were more common on Melanotan II.

src.label: Wessells H, et al. J Urol 1998

research.title: Men with ED and physical risk factors, 2000

facts.v: double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover; two injections of each
10 men with ED and physical risk factors
single doses; erections recorded for 6 hours
erections by RigiScan, sexual desire, side effects

research.found: Men reported erections after 12 of 19 Melanotan II injections and after 1 of 21 placebo doses. Reported sexual desire was higher after Melanotan II. Nausea and stretching or yawning were more common, and 4 of 19 injections caused severe nausea.

src.label: Wessells H, et al. Urology 2000

research.title: Melanotan II with light therapy for vitiligo (registered)

facts.v: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; added to narrowband UV-B light therapy
Hudson Biotech; site in Shenzhen, China

research.found: Recruiting since February 2026. No results posted. The registry summary describes itself as an “example” study record.

research.text: A PubMed search for “melanotan” finds about 250 papers; besides the studies above, most are animal studies, lab chemistry, surveys of use, and case reports. A ClinicalTrials.gov search finds only the vitiligo trial.

research.text: FDA says published case reports describe serious adverse events with Melanotan II, including melanoma, posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (a brain-swelling syndrome), sympathomimetic toxidrome (a racing, overstimulated state) and priapism.

src.label: FDA, bulk drug substances that may present significant safety risks (Category 2 page)

items.text: a 20-year-old woman who used Melanotan II injections with tanning beds for 3 to 4 weeks was found to have a melanoma three months later. Single case reports cannot show cause.

src.label: Hjuler KF, Lorentzen HF. Dermatology 2014

items.text: a 39-year-old man who injected 6 mg bought online had a fast heart rate, sweating, tremors and rhabdomyolysis, and spent 3 days in intensive care.

src.label: Nelson ME, et al. Clin Toxicol 2012

items.text: a man had a painful erection that would not go down after injecting melanotan. It needed draining and medicine into the penis, and his erections had not recovered 4 weeks later.

src.label: Dreyer BA, et al. BMJ Case Rep 2019

items.text: new and changing moles, a kidney infarction, and posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome.

us.text: Melanotan II is not FDA approved for any use. It is sold online labelled “for research use only” or “not for human consumption.” FDA does not allow such products to be sold for human use: it treats them as unapproved drugs. FDA lists Melanotan II among compounding nominations with significant safety risks that were later withdrawn. As of November 1, 2026.

items.text: none. Drugs@FDA has no record of a Melanotan II product.

items.text: FDA says companies that sell unapproved drugs labelled “for research purposes” or “not for human consumption,” directly to consumers for human use, are selling them illegally. FDA says SARMs “sold for research use only” are still unapproved drugs.

items.text: FDA’s page of bulk substances that may present significant safety risks lists Melanotan II among nominations that were withdrawn. FDA writes that compounded drugs containing it “may pose risk for immunogenicity” (an immune reaction) because of possible clumping or peptide impurities, and that “published case reports discuss serious adverse events including melanoma, posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome, sympathomimetic toxidrome and priapism.”

world.lead: Melanotan II is not an approved medicine in the US, Canada, the EU or Australia, as far as the records we opened show. Health Canada names it in a 2026 warning about unauthorized peptides. Australia lists it as a prescription-only substance.

after.text: Melanotan II is not named on the WADA 2026 Prohibited List. The list’s class S0 bans, at all times, any drug not covered by another class that has no current approval by any government health authority for human use. We found no such approval for Melanotan II, so S0’s wording would cover it, but WADA has not named it. The 2027 List, which takes effect January 1, 2027, adds “peptides” to S0’s examples.

side.text: The early studies reported nausea, yawning and stretching, less appetite, sleepiness, spontaneous erections and darker skin. Case reports since describe serious harms, including melanoma, priapism, muscle breakdown and a brain-swelling syndrome. There has never been a large safety study.
